title: Modeling Personality Traits by Predicting Questionnaire Responses as an Alternative Approach to Filipino Automatic Personality Recognition
venue: ACM International Conference on Asian Language Processing (IALP 2024)
tldr: Filipino APR using ML on social media data achieved modest improvements over baselines but revealed limitations in predicting personality from text in low-resource linguistic contexts.
problem_and_motivation: Automatic Personality Recognition (APR) using social media text is understudied in Filipino contexts despite the Philippines' high social media usage. Existing APR systems are limited by English-centric datasets, and the inherent noise and ambiguity of Filipino language pose challenges for text-based personality recognition.
approach: ML classification on Filipino Twitter/social media text using Bag-of-Words features (unigrams and bigrams) with Logistic Regression, SVM, Decision Trees, k-NN, and Naive Bayes. Filipinized personality questionnaires were used for ground-truth data collection. A hierarchical classification approach was introduced for Conscientiousness to improve prediction.
findings: Logistic Regression outperformed other models at 51.19% test accuracy, representing a 30% improvement over random baseline. Hierarchical classification improved Conscientiousness predictions. However, overall test performance remained very low, indicating that text-based APR in Filipino still requires significant advancement.

definitions.APR: Automatic Personality Recognition - systems that infer personality traits from behavioral or textual data
definitions.n-grams: Sequences of n consecutive words used as features in text classification
definitions.Bag-of-Words: Text representation method where document features are word frequencies ignoring grammar and word order
definitions.Filipinized questionnaires: Personality assessment instruments adapted/translated into Filipino language

limitations: Very low test metric scores across all models, indicating poor generalization
Data imbalance severely impacted model performance
Only English-Filipino bilingual subjects were used, limiting generalizability
Constrained dataset size due to limited availability of ground-truth data
Only two personality traits (Extraversion and Conscientiousness) were tested
remember_this: Filipino APR using traditional ML achieved modest gains over baselines but highlighted significant challenges in low-resource NLP for personality recognition. Hierarchical classification shows promise but requires further development.
